headline: High: Mentat’s broad network/file access can leak or act on code while the paired profile is only a non-runnable collection, so interaction risks are mostly one-sided but still material.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No plausible bidirectional prompt-injection pathway is documented. agent_a is a non-runnable collection with no I/O surfaces, while agent_b reads/writes files and uses stdin/stdout but there is no shared channel or default ingestion path from agent_a into agent_b.
conditions: IF agent_a is made runnable and its outputs are copied into agent_b inputs, injection risk appears.
IF a shared filesystem or clipboard bridge is introduced, agent_b may parse attacker-controlled content.
mitigations: Keep agent_a non-runnable.
Do not pipe agent_a output into agent_b prompts.
Disable shared clipboard/workspace bridges.
Review any copied text before pasting into agent_b.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging between tools.

B_data_leakage.rationale: agent_a touches no data classes and has no egress, while agent_b can read/write selected files and send context to a configured model provider. With no shared workspace documented, leakage is limited; if they are co-located on the same files, agent_b could expose code contents externally.
conditions: IF agent_a is given sensitive files and those files are passed to agent_b, code contents may leave the local environment.
IF both agents share a writable workspace, agent_b can read files that agent_a may reference.
mitigations: Keep sensitive files out of agent_b’s command-line inputs.
Use separate directories for each agent.
Restrict agent_b to non-sensitive repositories.
Rotate or scope model-provider keys for agent_b.
requires-engineering: enforce workspace isolation at the OS level.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: agent_a has no write or network capabilities, so it cannot contend for mutable resources. agent_b can write the filesystem and modify git state, but without a second writer in agent_a the overlap is minimal and not a default conflict pathway.
conditions: IF agent_a is replaced with a writable agent on the same repo, git/filesystem conflicts can occur.
IF multiple agent_b instances share the same filesystem without locking, edits may race.
mitigations: Run only one agent_b instance per workspace.
Avoid concurrent edits to the same repo.
Use separate git branches per task.
Check for uncommitted changes before each run.
requires-engineering: add file-locking or transactional edit coordination.

D_cascading_error.rationale: agent_a produces no actionable content, so agent_b has nothing authoritative to consume by default. If agent_a is repurposed to emit instructions or facts, agent_b’s diff-based edit workflow could propagate errors, but that pathway is not present in the current profiles.
conditions: IF agent_a begins emitting code or instructions that agent_b treats as authoritative, cascading errors become plausible.
IF agent_b is configured to apply diffs without human review, bad outputs can propagate.
mitigations: Keep human confirmation enabled for agent_b.
Do not feed agent_a outputs into agent_b as facts.
Require a review step before applying diffs.
Limit agent_b to small, isolated changes.
requires-engineering: add verification against source-of-truth data.

E_compliance.rationale: No residency or regulated-data mismatch is documented. agent_a has no touched data classes, while agent_b handles source code and model-provider API keys; the main compliance concern is ordinary code confidentiality, not a specific cross-border or PHI breach.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed in agent_b’s selected files, external model-provider transmission may create a compliance issue.
IF agent_a is later assigned regulated data, residency/retention review is required.
mitigations: Exclude regulated data from agent_b inputs.
Use a provider-approved environment for agent_b.
Review retention settings on the model provider.
Keep secrets out of editable files.
requires-engineering: document data-flow and residency controls.
